title: The Composition page, from route to editable slots
summary: `/muster` is a one-line server route onto `MusterPage`, a client component that loads the whole composition once and paints it as a tabbed console. A frozen readiness ledger sits under the header on every tab; the six section tabs mount only the active panel, so the heavy surfaces — Standing Fittings' slot cards and the routing-policy editor — fetch and render only when you open them, and each writes back with optimistic, no-Save-button autosave.

states.label: Composition
states.description: The drillbook asks that this page make the selected composition, its readiness, its duties, its targets, and the editing affordances understandable and usable — no visual collisions, no unexplained controls. It is the shell-owned surface where the whole system is configured, and it renders from one client component with per-tab panels.

steps.title: The route is a shim onto one client component
steps.description: Navigating to `/muster` lands on a server component that does nothing but mount `MusterPage`. There is no data-loading in the route itself — the eight-line file just returns the client component, which owns the fetch, the drag context and the autosave.

steps.title: A tablist over the composition, one panel mounted at a time
steps.description: `MusterPage` renders a tablist and a single stage. The active section is a piece of local state, and the stage is a chain of conditionals — only the matching panel mounts. That is deliberate: the heavy panels (Standing Fittings, the routing policy, the decisions feed) each own a separate fetch and only reach the network when their tab is opened, so the page is a focused single panel instead of one long scroll.

steps.title: The readiness pill is fixed above the tabs
steps.description: The command bar carries the composition's identity and one go/no-go pill driven straight off `model.ready` — Ready to run vs Not ready. It is rendered by `MusterHeader` alongside the composition switcher, and the full per-rule ledger (`ReadinessDetail`) sits under it always-mounted, not behind a tab, so run-readiness is visible the instant the page loads whatever section is open.

next.label: the Fittings tab lists what's stationed

steps.title: Standing Fittings is the 'what's stationed' surface
steps.description: The Fittings tab is the non-duty half of the page: one `SlotCard` per infrastructure faculty (channels, gateway, memory, observability, sessions, surfaces, connectors), each showing its stationed fitting(s), a config form and a Swap picker. This is the grid render — it maps the search-filtered slots to slot cards, wiring each slot's swap/remove/config/edit handlers so the operator can see and re-equip every slot from one view.

steps.title: The routing-policy editor autosaves with optimistic-concurrency safety
steps.description: The Orchestrator tab's Routing policy surface is the deepest editing affordance here: every committed edit debounces an 800ms whole-document PUT carrying a baseline sha. The response is the interesting part — a 409 means someone else moved the document (conflict banner, no write), and a 422 means the edit was rejected, so it reverts the draft to the last known-good config and surfaces why. There is no Save button; the concurrency guard is what makes silent autosave safe.
